sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. None appears on behalf of the respondent no.3 despite service of notice.
3. In terms of order dated 21.5.2024, the statement of the victim has been recorded under Section 35(1) of the POCSO Act.
4. As per the F.I.R., it was alleged that the physical relations were formed in between the applicant and the victim over a span of four years.
It was alleged that some inappropriate videos were made and subsequently when the victim married elsewhere, the photos were sent to the husband of the victim which resulted in divorce of the victim.

A somewhat similar statement was recorded before Haleem @ Mohd. Halim vs The State Of U.P. Thru. Prin.Secy. Home ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185327116/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the trial court.
However, in cross examination, the victim stated that these facts were not recorded as there was likelihood of the marriage being solemnised.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that admittedly the relationship between the victim and the applicant continues.
The is inordinate delay in lodging the F.I.R.
The tentative age of the victim is 15 years.
The determination of the tentative age of the victim shall be made by the trial court at the time of trial as per the mandate of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act.
Hence, the applicant who is languishing in jail since 11.3.2024 having criminal history of one case in which the applicant is on bail, may be enlarged on bail.
6. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.

7. Considering the fact that even as per admission of the parties, the relationship between the victim and the applicant and the tentative age of the age of the victim shall be decided by the trial court at the time of trial as per the mandate of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act and the applicant is languishing in jail since 11.3.2024 having criminal history of one case in which the applicant is on bail and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
8. Accordingly, the application for grant of bail is allowed.

9. Let the applicant Haleem @ Mohd. Halim be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.34 of 2024,
under Sections 376(3), 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4(2) of the POCSO Act and Section 66 (E) of the Information Technology Act, Police Station Matera, District Bahraich on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 13.8.2024/
